title: Distributed tagging and SLI attribution pipeline for multi-hop requests
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Add a lightweight distributed tagging layer and attribution pipeline so SLI measurements (latency/error) can be decomposed per business transaction across multi-hop requests. Current SLO signals are aggregated at service boundaries and lose caller context for long-tail transactions (e.g., chained reranking + fallback flows). This ticket implements tracing hooks at network ingress/egress, a tags-enrichment step in the metrics/log pipeline, and new SLI attribution rules to power per-route burn-rate alerts and targeted paging policies.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress and egress tracing hooks attach standardized transaction_id and route_tags to spans for 95% of traffic without increasing p50 latency by >2ms
Metrics pipeline adds 'transaction_id' and 'route_tags' labels to latency and error counters in the aggregator for sampled traces
We can compute per-transaction SLI time-series (error rate and p99 latency) in the metrics store with query latency < 5s for 30-day windows
New SLO decomposition dashboard shows top 20 transactions by burn-rate and direct links to traces/logs
Burn-rate alerts can be scoped to single transactions and trigger quieter paging policies (notify ops Slack only) when customer_impact is low
Regression test: synthetic long-chain transaction shows expected attribution across 3 services in staging and matches end-to-end trace
implementation_notes: Add a small tracing middleware in gateway and sidecars to set transaction_id if missing and propagate via B3/W3C headers
Use a compact stable key for route_tags (max 3 tags) to bound cardinality; initially include: product_area, api_route_group, priority_tier
In the metrics pipeline (ingesters), join sampled span data with request logs using trace_id or transaction_id; emit enriched metrics with low-cardinality route_tags
Avoid tagging every metric with full header metadata to prevent metric explosion; only attach tags to aggregated latency/error metrics used by SLOs
Store detailed mapping in a searchable trace-store for debug but keep metrics store dimensionality capped
Implement optional prefix-KV cache lookup to resolve route_group from path templates to reduce runtime cost
Anomaly detector should consume per-transaction SLI series and return attribution suggestions (service A vs service B) using simple residual analysis initially
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy hooks to gateway + one non-critical service, enable enrichment for sampled traffic only
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 10% production traffic, validate metric cardinality and storage growth
Phase 3 (gradual): expand to all services, enable full SLO decomposition and burn-rate alerting
Fallback: if metric cardinality or cost exceeds thresholds, revert enrichment and enable sample-based approximation
